pdf_metadata.Title: Do Short Exposure and Systematic Risk Exposure Drive Asymmetries in the Disposition Effect?

content_metadata.title: Do Short Exposure and Systematic Risk Exposure Drive Asymmetries in the Disposition Effect?
content_metadata.summary: This study examines the disposition effect in both long and short exposure positions in FTSE MIB-tracking ETFs, analyzing how portfolio context and systematic risk exposure affect investors' realization behavior. It finds that short positions exhibit a weaker disposition effect compared to long positions under narrow framing, which reverses in positively performing portfolios under integrated framing.
